Key.English: Lets players deploy forward operating bases, build them up from a supply count, and hold them. Enemy AI Commanders can find and attack them, and a FOB left undefended can be taken.
Place one Player FOBs module anywhere. It serves every side that has players. Each FOB becomes an objective for its own side's AI Commander, if that side has one.
Writes what the FOBs are doing to the RPT log.
Saves the FOBs, what's built at them and their supply with the mission, and puts them back when it's loaded. Needs an ALiVE Data module; without one they're kept in the server's profile instead.
How far from a FOB's headquarters players can build. Also the size of the objective the FOB becomes.
A new FOB can't be deployed closer than this to another FOB, of any side.
Dynamic: each side starts with Starting FOBs and earns one more for every Objectives Per FOB it holds, up to Most FOBs. Fixed: each side can have Fixed Limit FOBs.
How many FOBs each side can have when FOB Limit is Fixed, from 1 to 12.
With a dynamic limit, how many FOBs a side can have before it holds any ground.
With a dynamic limit, a side earns one more FOB for each this many objectives it holds. FOBs themselves don't count.
With a dynamic limit, the most FOBs a side can ever have.

What building and repairs are paid from. FOB supply: each FOB has its own supply count, topped up by Military Logistics. Force pool: the side's force pool, shared with the AI Commander and Recruitment. Supply crates: each FOB's count only rises when players unload supply crates at it.
The supply a new FOB starts with (FOB supply and supply crates). A FOB type can set its own (FOB Types).
Supply each FOB gains every minute on its own, with FOB supply. 0 for none. A FOB type can set its own (FOB Types).
The most supply a FOB of this tier can hold.
Every build cost is multiplied by this. 0.5 halves them, 2 doubles them.

The building each side's FOB starts with: lose it and the FOB is damaged until it's repaired. Side picks BLUFOR, OPFOR or Independent; Show lists military structures or every building. Click a building to tick or untick it: tick several and players choose one when they deploy a FOB.

The infantry group that garrisons each side's FOB from tier 2. Side picks BLUFOR, OPFOR or Independent; Show lists that side's groups or every side's. The first row, a random group of the FOB's faction, is the default.
(A random infantry group of the FOB's faction)
A building's class name, for one the list doesn't show, added to this side's ticked buildings when you leave the box. Several can be typed, separated by commas.
A group as faction/group, e.g. BLU_F/BUS_InfTeam, for one the list doesn't show; empty for a random group of the FOB's faction. What's here is this side's pick.

Yes: players can build an Arsenal at a FOB from tier 2, for 60 supply before the Cost Multiplier. It offers the infantry gear of every loaded mod, and whatever a player takes is charged to the FOB's supply when they close it. Gear handed back earns nothing. Build Only These, Never Build and CfgALiVEFOBBuildables can limit the gear and set its prices, as they do for the build menu. No: no Arsenal.
Yes: the FOB Arsenal also offers grenades, mines and explosive charges. No: it leaves them out.

Nothing to fill in here. This opens the FOB Build List in your browser: everything players can build, with its class name and cost. Put the class names you want in Never Build or Also Build, just below.

The object a FOB kit is, in place of the ALiVE kit box: one class name for every side, or one per side with the side first, for example WEST=B_CargoNet_01_ammo_F, EAST=O_CargoNet_01_ammo_F, GUER=I_CargoNet_01_ammo_F (WEST is BLUFOR, EAST OPFOR, GUER Independent; a side left out uses a class given without a side, if there is one). Empty (default) keeps the ALiVE kit, and a class the game doesn't have falls back to it.

The object a FOB supply crate is, in place of the ALiVE crate: one class name for every side, or one per side with the side first, for example WEST=B_CargoNet_01_ammo_F, EAST=O_CargoNet_01_ammo_F, GUER=I_CargoNet_01_ammo_F (WEST is BLUFOR, EAST OPFOR, GUER Independent; a side left out uses a class given without a side, if there is one). Empty (default) keeps the ALiVE crate.

A ready-made build list to start from, worked out from what each item is, so it suits any mod. Every preset keeps the fortifications and supplies. Never Build and Also Build still apply on top. A Build Only These list of objects replaces it; one naming only troops or gear leaves it in use.
Outpost: fortifications and supplies, no troops
Fortified Base: all but armour, artillery and aircraft
Infantry: troops, light static weapons, cars and trucks
Logistics Hub: supplies, trucks and boats, no troops

Class names separated by commas. When set, the Build Menu offers these and nothing else apart from Also Build, each priced by the module's own rules (as a fortification when the rules wouldn't pick it) unless CfgALiVEFOBBuildables gives a price. Add =price to set one here, such as Land_HBarrier_5_F=12. The Build List page on the ALiVE website writes this list for you. Never Build still applies. Soldier class names and group names are accepted too and go to the Troops tab: BUS_InfSquad means that group in every faction on your side, BLU_F>BUS_InfSquad one faction's. A list that names no troops leaves the Troops tab as it is, and one that names only troops leaves the other tabs as they are.

Class names players can never build, separated by commas, e.g. Land_Razorwire_F, B_MBT_01_cannon_F. Added to any CfgALiVEFOBBuildables blacklist. Soldier class names and group names are accepted too and keep them off the Troops tab: BUS_InfSquad means that group in every faction, BLU_F>BUS_InfSquad one faction's.

Class names to offer even though the Build Menu wouldn't pick them, separated by commas. They are offered even when Build Only These is set; Never Build still wins. They are priced as fortifications unless CfgALiVEFOBBuildables gives a price. Soldier class names and group names are accepted too and go to the Troops tab: BUS_InfSquad means that group in every faction on your side, BLU_F>BUS_InfSquad one faction's.

Who on the FOB's side may dismantle it, recycle what was built there and rename it. Tick as many as you like: any one of them lets a player in. Admins always can, so with nothing ticked only admins can. Admins can change this in game from the FOB window's Permissions button or the ALiVE admin menu.
Every player on the FOB's side. With this ticked the others make no difference.
A player who leads a group with at least one other player in it. Someone alone in a group of their own doesn't count.

The player who deployed that FOB, known by their player ID, so it still counts after they reconnect. A FOB saved before FOBs recorded this, or one taken from another side, lets in group leaders instead.

A unit class lets in every player in a slot of that class; a variable name lets in whoever takes that one slot.

How close, in metres, the enemy has to come before the FOB's side hears on the radio that it's under threat.

Seconds the enemy has to hold the FOB, unopposed, before it becomes theirs. Any defender in the capture radius starts the count again.

Supply to repair a destroyed headquarters at tier 1; one and a half times at tier 2, twice at tier 3. A quarter off with an engineer present.

Supply to upgrade a FOB to this tier. Tier 2 can hold more supply and builds towers, machine guns and grenade launchers; tier 3 holds the most, builds mortars, AT and AA launchers, vehicles, helicopters (on a helipad) and planes (at an airfield), and can be a respawn point.
From tier 1 (as soon as it's deployed)

In FOB Supply mode, a FOB below this share of its supply limit asks its side's Military Logistics for a supply truck, at most every 10 minutes. The truck brings a Supply Crate's worth. 0 turns it off. Needs a Military Logistics module for that side.

Whether enemy AI Commanders go after FOBs. Contact: once their men have found it (came within the Discovery Radius or shot at its headquarters). Immediate: from the moment it is deployed. Off: never. Insurgent commanders go after a FOB too; a strong garrison draws attacks rather than an assault.
With Contact targeting, enemy men inside this many metres of a FOB give it away to their side's commanders.
Vehicle, empty, for your side to crew
Aircraft, empty, for your side to crew. A helicopter goes on a helipad, a plane on an airfield taxiway or parking area

What one soldier raised from the Build Menu costs in FOB supply, before the Cost Multiplier. A group costs this for each of its men. Build Only These can set a price with =, such as BUS_InfSquad=400. In Force pool mode a soldier or a group costs 1 from its faction's pool, as a Combat Logistics requisition does.

How many soldiers players can raise at a FOB from the Build Menu's Troops tab, for each tier: 8 lets a tier 1 FOB hold 8, tier 2 16 and tier 3 24. Single soldiers can be raised from tier 1, groups from tier 2. Raised troops hold the FOB, never leave it, and are lost with it. 0 turns the Troops tab off.

Where players find the FOB actions: the scroll wheel, the ACE interaction menu (a Player FOBs entry in the self menu; Recycle and the Field HQ requests on the objects), or both. Auto uses ACE when ACE is loaded and the scroll wheel when it isn't.
Give the FOB a name of up to %1 characters.
Which items to list: what this FOB can build now, the items that need one tier, or every tier. Greyed items need a higher tier FOB.
Gives a FOB kit a choice of types, such as a fire base or a patrol base, each with its own headquarters buildings, build list, map marker, limit, cost and who may deploy it.

Place one and sync it to the Player FOBs module. Use the button to open the FOB Types editor in your browser and paste what it makes into Types. Not synced, it does nothing. A type changes what a FOB can build and who may deploy it, and can set its own respawn tier, starting supply and supply per minute; anything it leaves out, and the rest of how a FOB is supplied and upgraded, stays the Player FOBs module's settings.
Open the FOB Types editor (paste below)
Nothing to fill in here. This opens the FOB Types editor in your browser, which makes the text for Types, just below.

One type per line, each a set of key=value pairs separated by semicolons: id, name, prefix (the start of its FOBs' names, FOB by default), marker (a map marker class), hubs (headquarters classes, separated by commas), build (+class adds it, -class removes it; an added class no FOB could build before is kept for the types that add it), who (SIDE, LEADER or LIST, several separated by commas), list (player IDs, unit classes or Eden variable names, separated by commas, never semicolons), cost (taken when it's deployed), cap (most at once per side, 0 for no limit), respawn (the tier its respawn point comes at, 1 to 3, or 0 for none), supply (what a new one starts with, with FOB supply), trickle (supply per minute, with FOB supply) and role (not used yet). Respawn, supply and trickle left out use the Player FOBs settings. The FOB Types editor writes it for you.
